title: Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$
summary: Let $S = (S(n))$ be a simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ started at the origin. We study a loop-erasing procedure of $S[0,n]$ that differs from Lawler's chronological loop-erasure. Specifically, we remove loops from $S[0,n]$ in decreasing order of their lengths. The resulting random simple path is called the largest-loop-first (LLF) LERW. For $d=4$, we prove that the expected length of LLF LERW is of the order $n (\log n)^{-1/2 + o(1)}$.
